brief: Retrieve the signed archive copy from the Executive Vault. Oleg maintains the document archive. His personal account habits may be easier to recover than the documents he files.

facts.label: Archive directory
facts.note: His directory entry links a motoring forum and an obsolete access example. 'Nothing is lost. It is merely filed where nobody can find it.'

facts.label: Vehicle record
facts.note: His favourite car was built in 1984. He says he uses its make and full production year for memorable account strings.

facts.label: Motoring forum
facts.note: 'For the archive: make first, year next, then a #. It looks like a filing tag.' His signature links a message about the current car.

facts.label: Obsolete access
facts.note: The old year is wrong, but the name's capitalization and # suffix match the forum description.

facts.label: Current-car note
facts.value: Use the 1984 car, not the 1978 one
facts.note: Cross-reference confirms the current year and unchanged filing-tag suffix. 'Security is a system of labels. Mine has one label.'

facts.label: Fishing club
facts.note: A hobby, not an account hint. Even his fish prefer not to be documented.

solution.explanation: Oleg uses Volga with a capital V, followed by the current car's production year 1984, then #. The forum describes the order and suffix; the registry provides the year. Combine Volga and 1984 with the # suffix rule, or include # as a fragment.
